items.title: 东方诗意书法构成 × 实验水墨海报（3:4）
items.aspectNote: 源条目 3:4，Imagine 用 2:3 Poster。整批除 yishu-41 外都保持 2:3。
items.imaginePrompt:
A single full-bleed vertical 2:3 experimental Chinese calligraphy and ink-art poster — not a conventional poem-and-landscape illustration, not typography-only on a pure black field, and not a commercial title poster. Invent the complete work — do not ask for a reference image.

THEME: the classical couplet 「行到水穷处，坐看云起时」. The core mood is open, quiet, and contemplative: a path ending, then sitting to watch clouds rise. The visual action is extending, dissolving, and rising. Do not pile up generic antique props.

Calligraphy is the MAIN visual structure, not a caption on a painting. Let the characters themselves form mist, a receding stream, hanging willows or rising cloud. Some figurative forms may gradually become writing; dense small script may gather into a natural shape. From a distance, a complete poetic image; up close, real brush-written characters. Use running script, running-cursive, or cursive with genuine brush qualities: ligatures, hairline connections, thick-and-thin pressure, dry flying-white, ink bleed, broken and accidental marks. Allow some tilt, overlap, interruption, and a little correction. Mix large, medium and small scales — mostly fine dense script, with a few larger characters for rhythm. Local high-density columns of irregular length and direction; then sparse, broken, fading writing. No giant commercial headline, no neat centered poster lines, no mechanical computer fonts.

If heavy ink appears, it must fuse with the writing: ink that contains characters, characters that live inside the ink. Real xuan-paper edges, dry-wet changes, brush traces, flying-white, a little spatter. Large warm-white leftover paper as contrast. Optional: one very small figure (about 6 to 12 percent of the height) sitting and watching clouds, in restrained ink-figure style, not cartoon, not photoreal, not a large hero. Optional one or two tiny cinnabar seals. Palette: warm white, ivory, ink black, charcoal, ash; at most a hint of grey-green or pale ochre. No gold borders, no large red fields, no bright gradients.

The two key phrases 「行到水穷处」 and 「坐看云起时」 must be complete, correctly written, and readable wherever they appear as the larger characters. Prefer the cleaner, correctly written typography variant. If dense smaller script becomes illegible pseudo-characters, choose the variant where the main couplet is clearly correct. No logos, no watermarks, no decorative borders.

items.title: 摄影图形转译海报（动物轮廓 · 上下 3:4）
items.aspectNote: 源条目 3:4，Imagine 用 2:3 Poster。「上下 1:1」是竖版里上下各占 50%，不要切到 1:1 Square。画面禁止文字。
items.imaginePrompt:
A vertical 2:3 art poster strictly split 50/50 top and bottom, a clean natural join, no frames, titles, typography, logos, or watermarks. The source “1:1” means equal halves, not a square canvas. Invent one complete scene — do not ask for a reference photo.

TOP HALF: a photoreal photograph of a still koi pond in soft daylight — several orange-and-white koi just beneath the surface, a few lily pads, gentle ripples, mossy stone at the edge. Exhibition / magazine grade, only subtle film grain and editorial grading. Keep the subjects, count, composition, light, color, materials and space. Do not add, remove, duplicate or distort elements.

BOTTOM HALF: a large field of warm ivory art paper with generous leftover white. From this same pond, derive one clearly recognizable koi / carp contour — not a generic bird or deer template, not a flat color silhouette, not a simple icon, and not a hard-edged photo mask. The original photo’s texture, light and local details should flow naturally INSIDE the animal outline. Outside the contour, extend 4 to 6 translucent photographic slices with slight misregistration, stepped edges, frame-like overlays, local fade and a little overprint offset, so the photograph seems to spill out of the shape. The animal occupies about 48–55 percent of the lower width and 55–62 percent of the lower height, centered or slightly off-center, with ample warm-white space around it.

Mood: restrained, quiet, modern graphic design meeting photographic collage. Faint paper fiber, film grain, and print feel. Colors taken only from the photo. No typography of any kind, no realistic illustration, no cartoon, no 3D, no busy collage, no logos or watermarks.

items.title: 日式手绘漫画风对照海报（少色印刷 · 3:4）
items.imaginePrompt:
A vertical 2:3 comparison poster strictly split 50/50 top and bottom, same width, a clean straight horizontal join, no gap, outer frame, or overlap. Invent one complete scene — do not ask for a reference photo.

TOP HALF: an unaltered-looking photoreal photograph of a fully clothed adult East Asian woman in a grey wool coat and a mustard scarf, standing on an overcast train-platform with a paper bag in one hand, pale daylight, wet pavement, the platform edge visible. Editorial reportage grade. No typography on the photograph. Do not redraw or recolor the photo.

BOTTOM HALF: the SAME moment redrawn as a Japanese hand-drawn manga / limited-color print. Keep her face shape, hair silhouette, expression, pose, coat and scarf type, the bag, and the platform spatial relationships. Convert her into simple comic planes, bundled hair, and a clear fashion silhouette. Thin ink lines in near-black #02030B with natural pressure, pauses, and slight unevenness; interior lines only where structure turns. Flat, continuous, opaque color; shadows merged into a few hard-edged planes. No hair-by-hair texture, no dense hatch, no photoreal grain. Keep key local colors. Paper ground: pale grey-ivory #ECEDE5. Warm red #E9444B as the main accent (the scarf may carry it), a little grey-blue #5296BD in small areas, more red than blue. Simplify the background to the paper, keeping only what is needed to read the platform and the pose. Do not invent extra props.

Layout: treat the figure and the necessary environment as one group, scaled down and centered, about 65–70 percent of the lower width and 60–65 percent of the lower height, not stretched, not flush to the edges, no illustration frame, no color block filling the leftover paper. In the top leftover space, write small thin handwritten ink words: “FROM LIFE TO LINES.” Beside the drawing, even smaller casual ink words: “another way to see.” Prefer the cleaner typography variant; if lettering is messy, choose the cleaner one.

Distinct from an ugly-cute cartoon restyle, a cobalt-yellow commentary sticker, and a sparse editorial doodle. No logos or watermarks.

items.title: 明日方舟 SideStory「时间啊，向前！」塔露拉极简剧情海报（16:9）
items.aspectNote: 源条目 16:9，Imagine 用 16:9 Widescreen。生成前先切换，生成后立刻切回 2:3 Poster。
items.imaginePrompt:
A single full-bleed horizontal 16:9 minimal narrative poster in the visual language of Bauhaus political posters, revolutionary archive printing, and labor-movement prints: simple planar composition, a limited palette, strong geometric cuts, large leftover paper, coarse silkscreen, halftone dots, fibrous paper, uneven ink, and slight photocopy wear. Invent the complete scene — do not ask for a reference image. Do not name or cite any existing game, anime, or franchise, and do not use any official character name, logo, or trademark.

SUBJECT: an original tall, slender adult woman — not an official character from any game. Silver-white long hair, red eyes, black dragon horns, a long dragon tail, a black and deep-grey combat coat with dark-red details, and only her left arm (the right sleeve hangs empty). Keep this silhouette, coloring, adult age, and reserved temperament, but treat her as an original figure.

CAMERA: a strict ninety-degree vertical overhead view looking straight down from above her head — not a low angle, not from the feet up. She sits slightly right of center, her body on a slight diagonal across the width. From above you can read her silver hair, black horns, shoulders, arms, black coat and long tail, simplified into a clear flat geometric silhouette, not complex realistic perspective.

She is standing on early-spring melting snow, just risen and about to go on. One hand lightly holds the edge of her coat; the other hangs naturally. Not a combat pose: no sword, no magic effects, no victory gesture. Her expression is tired, clear, restrained and determined — grief after losing companions, but no tears, no rage, and no victor’s smile.

NARRATIVE LEFT TO RIGHT: the left is the past and memory; the center is the woman; the right is an unfinished future. LEFT: only a few abstract signs — several low, plain gravestones half-covered by thawing snow, three or four simplified birch branches, and a very faint early-farm-memory in low-contrast halftone, not a full scene and not a clear group portrait. A wooden hut, a campfire, and blurred companion silhouettes may be barely suggested, like a faded archive photograph. One companion may appear only as an extremely faint memory outline — not a solid body, not a ghost, no halo, and no interaction with the woman. RIGHT: a large field of pale grey unprinted paper, with only a little geometric shadow stretching right, melt-snow shapes, and simplified birch twigs. No road, no footprints, no full forest, city, battlefield, farm, or busy environment.

A deep-red ribbon runs across the whole width as the main geometric tension: entering from the gravestones and memory, passing near her head and shoulders, cutting diagonally behind her body, then crossing in front of her arm or coat edge, and exiting toward the right edge. The ribbon is a flat deep-red geometric shape, not realistic silk — sharp folds, changing width, triangular facets, sudden turns, local crops. Not a bow, not a romantic sash, not soft cloth. It must clearly layer with her: some parts behind hair, shoulder and tail, some narrow parts in front of the forearm or coat; where it meets her contour it is cut cleanly and continues on the far side along the same axis. Clean sharp paper-negative cuts — no glow, white outline, soft halo, or rectangular mask.

Near her, a very small dark red-orange ember as a flat printed emblem, not a huge flame, not a magic effect, not an explosion.

TYPOGRAPHY must fuse with the geometry, not float like digital stickers. Along the left edge, a huge vertical title “FORWARD”, rotated ninety degrees counterclockwise so it reads upward, in extremely heavy Bauhaus geometric sans: rectangular stems, semicircular counters, sharp cuts. Part of the word is covered by the red ribbon; part is cut by the gravestones and grey blocks. The first letter is deep red; the remaining letters are graphite black. The type shares the same halftone, ink wear and print offset as the ground. In the upper-right or right leftover area, three stacked lines: “TIME” / “TO” / “MOVE”. “TIME” and “TO” in graphite on a pale grey block; “TO” partly covered by a slanted red ribbon; “MOVE” in black on a deep-red rectangle connected to the ribbon. Only these words — no other captions. Prefer the cleaner typography variant.

Palette only: pale warm-grey paper, ivory, graphite black, deep grey, low-saturation blue-grey, deep red, dark red-orange, and a tiny bit of sulfur yellow. Low-saturation, cold, restrained. Warm color only on the ribbon and the small ember. No bright gradients, neon, or high-saturation fantasy color. No logos, watermarks, or official franchise marks.

items.title: ABOVE THE GRID｜电力线路检修海报（英文 · 包豪斯 × 半调拼贴）
items.aspectNote: 源条目 3:4，Imagine 用 2:3 Poster。生成前确认已切回 2:3 Poster。这是满版竖构图海报，不是双联。
items.imaginePrompt:
A single full-bleed vertical 2:3 electrical-line maintenance poster combining Bauhaus geometric typography, overhead infrastructure diagrams, desaturated photographic halftone collage, and deliberate negative-space printing. A tall narrow composition on cold gray paper, with deep electric-blue conductor graphics, graphite-black steelwork, and sparse sulfur-yellow accents. Invent the complete scene — do not ask for a reference photo. Distinct from a 16:9 snow-and-red-ribbon narrative poster.

Along the far-left edge, the enormous word “POWER”, rotated ninety degrees counterclockwise to read upward. Letters built from heavy rectangular stems, semicircular counters, and sharp geometric cuts. The first letter in electric blue, the remaining letters in graphite black. Partially crop the uppermost letter against the top boundary.

In the upper-right quadrant, the exact stacked headline:
ABOVE
THE
GRID
Exceptionally heavy uppercase geometric display lettering. The first two lines in graphite; the final word in black inside a small sulfur-yellow rectangular field. Keep the lettering clear of the principal conductor paths. Prefer the cleaner typography variant; if letters are garbled, choose the cleaner one.

A strict ninety-degree overhead camera looking vertically downward onto the worker, cables, and tower, a true view from directly above the helmet, with strong top-down foreshortening: the helmet and shoulders conceal parts of the torso. A substantial fragment of a high-voltage steel lattice tower is cropped into the upper-left area and top edge: interconnected braces, part of a crossarm, compact insulator assemblies; the tower continues outside the frame.

Three parallel conductor paths run from the top edge all the way to the bottom. Their direction on the page is vertical, axes aligned and visually continuous. Fine charcoal cable edges combined with selected flat electric-blue bands, a clear vertical rhythm.

Exactly one adult electrical maintenance worker near the lower-middle, overlapping the central conductor path, suspended just beneath a compact service trolley attached to the conductor, on a visible work harness with short tensioned connections. Compact seated suspension: torso angled diagonally across the vertical cable axis, both knees bent. From above, show the helmet crown, shoulders, forearms, harness, and foreshortened boots. One gloved hand steadies the trolley frame; the other rests near the tool pouch. Figure in strongly desaturated charcoal, dusty gray, muted grey-beige, and silver-white. Pale protective helmet, dark work clothing, gloves, clearly separated harness straps. Face hidden by the overhead viewpoint.

The worker–conductor overlap is the principal negative-space device. Wherever the dark cable lines and blue bands intersect the worker, knock out the corresponding helmet, shoulder, arm, or body contour to the unprinted gray-white paper. The conductor ink stops precisely at these human contours and resumes on the same axis beyond them. Inside the dark bands, the worker reads as a clean paper-white silhouette cut through the vertical pattern. Outside the overlap, keep the desaturated photographic figure and its halftone detail. Crisp ink subtraction — no soft glow, white outline, or rectangular mask.

Sparse infrastructure graphics: fine crossarm alignment marks, a few insulator-inspired outlined shapes, pale hatched sectors, and small sulfur-yellow index blocks. Any distant ground traces are extremely faint and still viewed from above. Include only the compact labels “LINE” and “ACCESS”.

Finish with fibrous gray paper, fine speckles, uneven blue ink, restrained photocopy abrasion, and slightly degraded photographic edges. Preserve the clean negative-space intersections. No horizon, no frontal face, no oblique camera, no falling pose, no detached harness, no extra workers, no lightning, no surrounding frame, no watermark, no logos.
